title: Unclosed engineering and trust gaps
summary: Native file output proves byte ordering and queue semantics, but production browser calls need end-to-end timing, live device formats, failure recovery, audio routing, presentation grants, redaction and an auditable session lifecycle.
invariants: Do not conflate a static /dev/video0 file handle with confirmed WebRTC media delivery.
Do not infer exact A/V skew from fixed frame counts; measure both output and receiver timelines.
Do not use a demo-only grant to publish private invoices, statuses, reports or customer identities.
Do not treat a file-size preflight as prevention of a same-size race or content substitution.
No live encrypted RTP/WebRTC driver is implemented here; the browser owns its own capture stack.
procedure: Add content-addressed or immutable staged-asset input and bounded resource guarantees.
Implement time-bounded PresentationGrant before real customer traffic.
Measure monotonic playout drift, device backpressure, microphone levels, browser FPS and remote receiver skew.
Define fallback visuals/audio for device loss, stalled decode, denial and session termination.

provenance.claim: Known limitations and remaining live qualification.
